title: Formal fibres of A[x] over nonzero primes above (0), A complete local domain of characteristic p
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local domain which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and whose fraction field $K=A_{(0)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] has characteristic $p$. Let $A[x]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $\mathfrak q\subset A[x]$ a maximal ideal with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$ a prime ideal with $\mathfrak r\ne(0)$ and $\mathfrak r\cap A=(0)$. Let $\kappa(\mathfrak r)=A[x]_{\mathfrak r}/\mathfrak rA[x]_{\mathfrak r}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(A[x]_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA[x]_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^nA[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ the completion of the local ring $A[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then the $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$-algebra $(A[x]_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494) and its proof (Algebra Lemma Tag 07N9 completion-finite-extension; More on Algebra Lemmas 07PE derivation-extends, 07EC formally-smooth, 07ED formally-smooth-completion, Proposition 07PM fs-regular, Lemma 07PF quotient-regular)

proof.text: (Completed local rings of $B[x]$.) Let $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be any Noetherian local ring which is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $\mathfrak Q\subset B[x]$ a maximal ideal with $\mathfrak Q\cap B=\mathfrak n$, $T=B[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$ and $C_{\mathfrak Q}=T^\wedge=\varprojlim_nT/\mathfrak Q^nT$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. $B[x]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], hence so is $T$ (every ideal of $T$ is generated by the image of an ideal of $B[x]$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak QT$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. So $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak QC_{\mathfrak Q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and complete for it: by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (with the finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak QT$ and $M=T$) $C_{\mathfrak Q}\to\varprojlim_nC_{\mathfrak Q}/\mathfrak Q^nC_{\mathfrak Q}$ is bijective. The composite $B\to B[x]\to T\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a local homomorphism since $\mathfrak n\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ maps into $\mathfrak QC_{\mathfrak Q}$. For every prime $\mathfrak s$ of $B[x]$ the fibre ring $C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian] (applied to $B[x]\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$). In particular (with $B=A$, $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak r$) the ring $F=C\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, $C=(A[x]_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$, is Noetherian.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494); the Noetherian completion facts are implicit in the source (they are the hypotheses of Proposition 07PM used in its second paragraph)

proof.text: (The residue field of a prime over $(0)$.) Let $B$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K_B=B_{(0)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $W=B\setminus\{0\}$, and $\mathfrak s\subset B[x]$ a prime with $\mathfrak s\ne(0)$ and $\mathfrak s\cap B=(0)$. The localization $\lambda:B[x]\to W^{-1}B[x]$ is $K_B[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] (a polynomial over $K_B$ is $g/w$ with $g\in B[x]$ and $w\in W$ a common denominator), and $\lambda$ is injective. As $\mathfrak s\cap W=\emptyset$, $\mathfrak sK_B[x]$ is a prime of $K_B[x]$ with $\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak sK_B[x])=\mathfrak s$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](1), and it is nonzero since $\mathfrak s\ne0$. $K_B[x]$ is a principal ideal domain (division with remainder by a nonzero polynomial over a field), so $\mathfrak sK_B[x]=gK_B[x]$ with $g$ monic irreducible of degree $d\ge1$ (a nonzero constant is a unit), and this ideal is maximal (if $(g)\subseteq(h)$ then $h\mid g$, so $h$ is a unit or an associate of $g$). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](3), $\kappa(\mathfrak s)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak sK_B[x])=K_B[x]/(g)$ as $B[x]$-algebras (for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$ of a ring $P$, $P_{\mathfrak M}/\mathfrak MP_{\mathfrak M}=P/\mathfrak M$ since $P/\mathfrak M$ is already a field). Hence $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ has $K_B$-basis $1,x,\dots,x^{d-1}$: $K_B\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is a finite extension of degree $d$, and $K_B\to\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is bijective iff $d=1$, i.e. iff $\mathfrak sK_B[x]=(x-f)$ for some $f\in K_B$. Finally, for any $B[x]$-algebra $E$, $E\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak s)\cong(E\otimes_{B[x]}K_B[x])\otimes_{K_B[x]}K_B[x]/(g)$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], $E\otimes_{B[x]}K_B[x]=W^{-1}E$ is the localization of $E$ at the image of $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], and $M\otimes_PP/(g)=M/gM$ (right exactness of $\otimes$); so $E\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak s)\cong W^{-1}E/g\,W^{-1}E$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494), first sentence ('Note that K subset kappa(r) is finite') and second paragraph ('r K[x] is generated by x - f for some f in K' and the displayed formula for the fibre); details written out

proof.text: (Claim: the case $K_B=\kappa(\mathfrak s)$.) Let $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian local domain, $\mathfrak n$-adically complete, with fraction field $K_B$, $\mathfrak Q\subset B[x]$ maximal with $\mathfrak Q\cap B=\mathfrak n$, and $(0)\ne\mathfrak s\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ a prime with $\mathfrak s\cap B=(0)$ such that $K_B\to\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is bijective. Claim: $C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Proof. By Step 2 $\mathfrak sK_B[x]=(x-f)$ with $f=a/w$, $a\in B$, $w\in W=B\setminus\{0\}$, and $C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak s)\cong R/(\iota(x)-f)R$, where $R=W^{-1}C_{\mathfrak Q}$ and $\iota:B[x]\to R$ is the canonical map. (i) $R$ is regular. By Step 1, $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a Noetherian local ring complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak QC_{\mathfrak Q}$ and $B\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a local homomorphism of complete Noetherian local rings; $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is formally smooth over $B$ for the $\mathfrak QC_{\mathfrak Q}$-adic topology [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-local-completion-formally-smooth] [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Hence $B\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a regular ring map [lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular]; its fibre over the prime $(0)$ of $B$, $C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_B\kappa((0))=C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_BK_B$, is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $K_B$, so taking $k'=K_B$ in the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] it is a regular ring. Now $C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_BK_B$ and $R=C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_{B[x]}K_B[x]$ are both localizations of $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ at the image of $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (applied to $B\to W^{-1}B$ and to $B[x]\to W^{-1}B[x]$), hence isomorphic as $C_{\mathfrak Q}$-algebras by the universal property of localization; so $R$ is regular. (ii) A derivation. $\partial=d/dx$ is a derivation of $B[x]$ (Leibniz rule for polynomials) with $\partial(B)=0$ and $\partial(x)=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends](2) it extends to $T=B[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$, by (1) to the $\mathfrak QT$-adic completion $C_{\mathfrak Q}$, compatibly with the canonical maps, and by (2) again to $R=W^{-1}C_{\mathfrak Q}$; call the result $D$. By construction $D\circ\iota=\iota\circ\partial$, so $D(\iota(b))=0$ for $b\in B$, and by the formula of (2), $D(\iota(a)/\iota(w))=D(\iota(a))/\iota(w)-\iota(a)D(\iota(w))/\iota(w)^2=0$. Hence $D(\iota(x)-f)=\iota(\partial x)=1$, a unit, in particular a unit modulo $(\iota(x)-f)R$. (iii) By [lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular] applied to the regular ring $R$, the element $\iota(x)-f$ and $D$, the ring $R/(\iota(x)-f)R\cong C_{\mathfrak Q}\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is regular.

proof.text: (A finite extension $B$ realizing $L$.) Let $L/\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (possibly $L=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$). By Step 2 (with $B=A$, $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak r$) $K\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is finite, so $L/K$ is finite (degrees multiply). Let $l_1,\dots,l_s$ be a $K$-basis of $L$. Each $l_j$ is a root of a monic polynomial $X^{N}+c_{1}X^{N-1}+\dots+c_{N}$ with $c_i\in K$ ($1,l_j,\dots,l_j^{N}$ are linearly dependent for $N=[L:K]$; divide by the leading coefficient); choose $\delta\in A\setminus\{0\}$ with $\delta c_i\in A$ for all coefficients of all $j$; then $e_j=\delta l_j$ is a root of $X^N+\delta c_1X^{N-1}+\delta^2c_2X^{N-2}+\dots+\delta^Nc_N\in A[X]$, so it is integral over $A$. Let $B=A[e_1,\dots,e_s]\subseteq L$: a domain, a finitely generated $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], whose fraction field (inside $L$) contains $K$ and $l_j=e_j/\delta$, hence equals $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] $B$ is a Noetherian local domain, complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_B$, and $\mathfrak n_B$ is the only prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak m$. Let $\xi\in\kappa(\mathfrak r)\subseteq L$ be the image of $x$ and $\rho:B[x]\to L$ the ring map which is the inclusion on $B$ and sends $x\mapsto\xi$; its kernel $\mathfrak r'$ is a prime ($L$ is a field). On $A[x]\subseteq B[x]$, $\rho$ is the composite $A[x]\to\kappa(\mathfrak r)\subseteq L$ (both are the inclusion on $A$ and send $x$ to $\xi$). Hence $\mathfrak r'\cap B=(0)$ ($\rho$ is injective on $B$) and $\mathfrak r'\ne(0)$ (a nonzero $g\in\mathfrak r\subseteq A[x]\subseteq B[x]$ maps to $0$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$). The image $\rho(B[x])=B[\xi]$ is a subring of $L$ containing $B$, so its fraction field is $L$; as $\kappa(\mathfrak r')=B[x]_{\mathfrak r'}/\mathfrak r'B[x]_{\mathfrak r'}$ is the fraction field of the domain $B[x]/\mathfrak r'\cong B[\xi]$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\rho$ induces an isomorphism of $B[x]$-algebras $\kappa(\mathfrak r')\cong L$, under which $K_B=L\to\kappa(\mathfrak r')$ is bijective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494), first paragraph ('given a finite purely inseparable extension L/kappa(r) there exists a finite extension of Noetherian complete local domains A subset B ... you take B subset L a finite A-subalgebra whose field of fractions is L. Denote r' subset B[x] the kernel ... so that kappa(r') = L'); B complete local: Algebra Lemma 0325

proof.text: (Decomposition.) $A[x]\to B[x]$ is finite: if $B=\sum_iAb_i$ then $B[x]=\sum_iA[x]b_i$; $A[x]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Let $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ be the primes of $B[x]$ lying over $\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] (with $R=A[x]$, $S=B[x]$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q$) there is an isomorphism of $B[x]$-algebras $C\otimes_{A[x]}B[x]\cong\prod_{i=1}^t(B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$. Regard $L$ as an $A[x]$-algebra via $A[x]\to\kappa(\mathfrak r)\to L$, which by Step 4 equals $A[x]\to B[x]\xrightarrow{\rho}L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] twice (with $A[x]\to\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ and with $A[x]\to B[x]$): $L\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak r)}F=L\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak r)}(\kappa(\mathfrak r)\otimes_{A[x]}C)\cong L\otimes_{A[x]}C\cong L\otimes_{B[x]}(B[x]\otimes_{A[x]}C)\cong L\otimes_{B[x]}\prod_i(B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge\cong\prod_i(B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r')$, using that $\otimes$ commutes with finite products and $L\cong\kappa(\mathfrak r')$ as $B[x]$-algebras (Step 4).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494), first paragraph, displayed formula 'A[x]_q^ (x)_{A[x]} L = A[x]_q^ (x)_{A[x]} B[x] (x)_{B[x]} kappa(r') = prod B[x]_{q_i}^ (x)_{B[x]} kappa(r')' with Algebra Lemma 07N9 (completion-finite-extension)

proof.text: (Each factor is regular.) Each $\mathfrak q_i$ is maximal: $B[x]/\mathfrak q_i$ is a domain containing the field $k_0=A[x]/\mathfrak q$ and a finitely generated $k_0$-module, hence integral over $k_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; for $0\ne y$ in it, $y^{-n}+d_1y^{-n+1}+\dots+d_n=0$ ($d_j\in k_0$, $y^{-1}$ taken in the fraction field) gives $y^{-1}=-(d_1+d_2y+\dots+d_ny^{n-1})$, so it is a field. $\mathfrak q_i\cap B$ is a prime of $B$ whose inverse image in $A$ is $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak q_i\cap B=\mathfrak n_B$ by Step 4. If $\mathfrak r'\not\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$, pick $u\in\mathfrak r'\setminus\mathfrak q_i$: $u$ is a unit in $B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i}$, hence in $(B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$, and $u$ acts as $0$ on $\kappa(\mathfrak r')$, so in $(B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r')$ we get $1\otimes1=u^{-1}\otimes u\cdot1=0$: the factor is the zero ring, which is regular (it has no prime ideals) [def-weil-regular-scheme]. If $\mathfrak r'\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$, the Claim of Step 3 applies to $(B,\mathfrak n_B)$, $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak q_i$ and $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak r'$ (a nonzero prime with $\mathfrak r'\cap B=(0)$ and $K_B=L\to\kappa(\mathfrak r')$ bijective, Step 4): the factor $(B[x]_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge\otimes_{B[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r')$ is regular.

This reduces us to ... the special case that K = kappa(r)'); the verification of the hypotheses on q_i and r' and the case r' not in q_i are written out (the source leaves them implicit)

proof.text:
(Conclusion.) A finite product $P=\prod_{i=1}^tR_i$ of regular rings is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]: with the idempotents $e_i$ ($\sum e_i=1$, $e_ie_k=0$ for $i
e k$), every ideal $I$ of $P$ is $\prod_ie_iI$, so $P$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; a prime $\mathfrak P$ contains all $e_k$ but exactly one $e_j$ (as $e_ie_k=0\in\mathfrak P$ and $1
otin\mathfrak P$), so $\mathfrak P=R_1	imes\dots	imes\mathfrak P_j	imes\dots	imes R_t$ with $\mathfrak P_j$ a prime of $R_j$, and $P_{\mathfrak P}\cong(R_j)_{\mathfrak P_j}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] ($e_j$ becomes a unit, hence $1$, and each $e_k$, $k
e j$, becomes $0$), a regular local ring. By Steps 5 and 6, $L\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak r)}F$ is regular for every finite purely inseparable extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, and $F$ is Noetherian by Step 1. Hence $F=(A[x]_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. (The hypothesis that $K$ has characteristic $p$ is not used; it records the case in which the source applies the lemma.)
